C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY.Summary: Deliver RM-GOVERNED-PATH P1 steps 13 and 14 only: make lint reject an XML comment that is not well-formed under XML 1.0 section 2.5 (two adjacent hyphen characters inside the comment body) on every artifact parseGraceXmlArtifact already reads, with a forward check proved on fixtures rather than by grandfathering the archived offenders; and interpolate the requested text and the subject file into assertion.MustContain / assertion.MustNotContain failure messages, with MustNotContain also naming the first-hit offset, on the issue message field that both the text report and --format json already print.
C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY.Problem:
**Shared shape.** Two P1 items are the same class of change in the same layer: the product knows a fact and declines to say it on an agent-facing surface. P1's objective is that an agent learns the fix from the error. Sequencing them together is the same-layer dependency F39 recorded, not a convenience. Authoring HEAD `93a9062`, packaged 6.2.0, lint 0/0, active changes empty.
---
**P1.13 — lint accepts artifacts that are not well-formed XML.** `ngrace lint` reports every artifact clean while a conformant parser rejects several. Cause is uniform: two adjacent hyphen characters inside an XML comment, which XML 1.0 section 2.5 forbids, `fast-xml-parser` / `XMLValidator.validate` accept, and expat rejects. `parseGraceXmlArtifact` therefore returns a root and zero `xml.parse` issues. The product's own parser reads the files; nothing is broken today. What is false is the report line `XML artifacts checked` / `Errors: 0`, which claims a validity never checked (F10 at the tool level).
Re-measured at this HEAD: **9** artifacts, all archived `plan.xml` (survey, not a criterion — F33 / F39.1: the set grows). The ninth is `C-GRAMMAR-SEAM`'s archived plan, written by an executor that had read F39, named it, and stated it was avoiding the sequence in comments. A long DESIGN block about a CLI gives the hazard dozens of chances; care has to win every time. A repair that only grandfathers the archive and adds no forward check leaves the count climbing (F39.1).
`xml.parse` already exists. It fires when `XMLValidator.validate` rejects the document or the parse yields no root — unreadable input. It does not fire on these nine. Reusing that code for a document that parsed successfully would make the code name claim more than the body verifies (F10 / F52). A new constructed `xml.*` code needs an exact guide or the P1.1–3 coverage test fails (F27.2).
Archive treatment is **not assumed**. The four options, their costs, which have F28 shape, and the recommendation live in Assumptions. Criteria bind the forward check.
---
**P1.14 — assertion.MustContain withholds the text it asked for.** `evaluateTextContainment` in `src/artifact/assertions.ts` holds the requested text and interpolates only the subject file: the failure message is the file, then "must contain requested text" or "must not contain requested text." A plan that pins one file seven times produces seven identical lines. The same string is the JSON `message`; `NgraceIssue` and `LintIssue` have no `detail` field (F40's empty-detail observation is that hole, not a missing key to invent). The sibling `MustMatchPattern` already interpolates its subject via `JSON.stringify`. This is P1's objective failing in its purest form, the same class as P0.7 and `C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE`, on a surface neither reached.

Goals.Goal: **P1.13 forward check.** A fixture artifact whose XML comment body contains two adjacent hyphen characters emits a dedicated well-formedness error at error severity. A fixture whose comments omit that sequence does not emit it. The check runs on every artifact parseGraceXmlArtifact already reads, not on change bundles only. The archived nine are not this goal's evidence.

**P1.13 teaching.** That diagnostic names the forbidden sequence, that it sits inside an XML comment, and the repair (rewrite the comment body so it does not contain the sequence), as the first shape it names. The exact guide for that code teaches the same and does not describe the document as unreadable.

**P1.14 visible subject.** On the containment-failure path only, the issue `message` names the subject file as its first token, then the requested text after the verb, quoted as `JSON.stringify` quotes the sibling pattern assertions. MustNotContain also names the first-hit offset last on that message. Codes stay `assertion.MustContain` and `assertion.MustNotContain`.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-XML-COMMENT-WELL-FORMED: A fixture artifact that parseGraceXmlArtifact reads, whose only well-formedness defect is two adjacent hyphen characters inside an XML comment body, produces `xml.comment-not-well-formed` at error severity and still returns a root. A fixture whose comments omit that sequence does not emit that code. One sample document kind does not satisfy the set: plant at least a change plan and one non-plan artifact (a context or graph document). Two adjacent hyphens in element text are legal and must not emit the code. The archived nine are not this criterion's evidence. Archive treatment of those nine is Assumptions, not this bind. **HEAD today:** `XMLValidator.validate` accepts the sequence; `parseGraceXmlArtifact` returns a root and zero issues on a comment-body plant; lint on this repository reports the nine archived plans clean. **Failure conditions:** only plans planted; check implemented only on active bundles and sold as this criterion; `xml.parse` reused while a root exists; root dropped so other diagnostics vanish; element-text hyphens rejected; the nine archived files cited as the red; a count of nine frozen as the pass bar.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-COMMENT-ERROR-TEACHES: The `xml.comment-not-well-formed` `message` names three things, in this order (F44): that the defect is inside an XML comment; that the forbidden content is two adjacent hyphen characters; the repair (rewrite the comment body so it does not contain that sequence). A later mention after a "document failed to parse" instruction does not satisfy. This criterion binds that semantic content; the test asserts the literal bytes. **HEAD today:** no such code exists; the nine files emit no well-formedness message. **Failure conditions:** only the code token asserted; working form named after an unreadable-document instruction; `--explain` cited while the emitted message still withholds the sequence or the comment location; this criterion treated as a quoted-byte bind in this file.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-COMMENT-GUIDE-TEACHES: The `lint --explain` exact guide for `xml.comment-not-well-formed` names the same three facts as AC-COMMENT-ERROR-TEACHES, as the first shape it names, and does not describe the document as unreadable. The `xml.parse` exact guide is not a member and is not rewritten. This criterion binds semantic content; the test asserts the rendered guide bytes. **HEAD today:** the code is absent, so it cannot classify as exact; `xml.parse` is exact and speaks to unclosed tags, bad entities, or a missing root. **Failure conditions:** only the emitted message cited; `xml.parse` guide rewritten as if it were a member; catalog restructured; the resolution-path predicate edited; an exact guide C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE authored rewritten.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CONTAINMENT-MESSAGE: On the containment-failure path, `evaluateTextContainment` issues have code `assertion.MustContain` or `assertion.MustNotContain` (the mapping does not move — F48). `message` starts with the subject file token, then the verb, then the requested text as `JSON.stringify` of that string. For MustNotContain, `message` ends with a parenthetical first-hit offset that equals `indexOf` of that text in the file string the evaluator read. MustContain has no offset (there is no hit). Two MustContain failures on the same file with different texts produce two distinguishable `message` values. Missing-field, missing-file, and not-a-regular-file paths are not members. Text-report and JSON display of `message` are the same field (F45: the display half is true by construction once `message` is repaired; do not redden it). This criterion binds that shape; the test asserts the literal bytes. **HEAD today:** MustContain message is the file plus "must contain requested text"; MustNotContain is the file plus "must not contain requested text"; neither interpolates the text; JSON `message` is that same string; `assertions.test.ts` asserts the codes, not those message bytes. **Failure conditions:** only MustContain repaired; text interpolated but after an instruction that still says "requested text" as the first named subject; offset given as a line number or a UTF-8 byte count the evaluator did not compute; a new `detail` field added instead of repairing `message`; codes renamed; display-half JSON asserted as the HEAD-RED.

Assumptions.Assumption: **Authoring HEAD `93a9062`, packaged 6.2.0, lint 0/0.** Active changes were empty before this bundle. F33: implementation re-measures counts; criteria do not freeze the nine or any line number.

**Survey snapshot, not a criterion.** Re-measured at this HEAD: nine archived plans contain the forbidden sequence inside an XML comment, and no other `.ngrace/**/*.xml` does:
C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE, C-DECLARED-WRITES, C-ESCALATION-HONESTY, C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT, C-FLAG-HONESTY, C-GRAMMAR-SEAM, C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE, C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE, C-REPORT-HONESTY
— each `plan.xml` only. `xml.parse` exact guide exists. `assertion.MustContain` / `assertion.MustNotContain` have no exact guides (prefix `assertion.`). `NgraceIssue` / `LintIssue` have fields severity, code, file, optional line, message — no `detail`. `MustMatchPattern` already interpolates via `JSON.stringify`.

**Archive treatment — options, costs, F28, recommendation.** Authority chooses. Criteria bind only the forward check. Until a different pick is written into an approved spec, the plan implements the recommendation.
**Option 1 — scope the check to active bundles only.** Cost: a 10th offender under archive (a new archived spec, a copied plan, any non-plan archive file) is silent. Non-bundle artifacts that are not "active bundles" are out of the check unless separately included. This repository's close bar stays 0/0. F28 shape: **yes, if the nine are the claimed evidence** — they are excluded by class, which is exactly "a check that quietly excludes the files that motivated it." Not F28 if the evidence is a fixture and the exclusion is disclosed. Weaker forward check than option 3.
**Option 2 — warn on archive, error on active.** Cost: the nine become standing warnings on every `ngrace lint --path .` of this dogfood tree. AC-SUITE-AND-LINT's 0/0 at close is then unsatisfiable without weakening the close bar or ignoring archive warnings. Downstream projects without this archive pay nothing. F28 shape: **no** — the nine are visible. F52 shape: calling that "well-formedness is checked" while archive is only a warning is weaker than the name. Rejected for this repository because it collides with the 0/0 close bar this roadmap actually uses.
**Option 3 — frozen path allowlist of the nine; every other artifact errors.** Cost: the nine stay silent; the allowlist is product data that must be the re-measured paths, not the number nine (F33). A 10th path, including a new archived file, errors. 0/0 is preserved. F28 shape: **yes, if silence on the nine is sold as the red**; **no, if the red is a fixture and the allowlist is a named exception with a reason (archive immutability)**. Stronger forward check than option 1 (archive is not a blanket hole).
**Option 4 — re-examine archive immutability and repair the nine comments.** Cost: punches a hole in a wall this repository has used as a hard stop (CLAUDE.md, every recent bundle). Comment-only edits still rewrite approved historical artifacts. P3.2 already schedules `ngrace plan amend` as the controlled hatch. Doing it here pre-empts that hatch and creates a precedent the next bundle will cite. Combined with a uniform error check it is complete, and 0/0 holds after the repair. F28 shape: **no**. Conflict: archive immutability vs this class of repair. D11: not this bundle.
**Recommendation: option 3.** Forward-complete, preserves 0/0, does not pre-empt P3.2, and avoids option 1's blanket archive hole. F28 is discharged by fixture reds (AC-HEAD-RED) plus a test that a path not on the allowlist errors — not by the nine staying quiet. Option 2 is the honest visibility option and is incompatible with this repo's close bar; say so rather than ship nine eternal warnings. Option 4 is the honest cleanup and belongs to P3.2.
